why: The other half of the same line: the scaling stays and the floor goes, so a profile authored with a short enough delay resolves at `hard` to a picture current to the tick -- the oracle both #223 and #267 forbid by name ("never oracle-perfect"). It cannot be caught with the shipped profiles, whose 0.1s is nowhere near MIN_COMPETENCE_AWARENESS_DELAY at any preset, which is why the test probes a synthetic profile already at the bound -- the same argument bot-difficulty.test.ts's own oracle test makes for the accuracy ceiling. Killed by the one test that carries that fixture, which also checks the shipped profile still reaches a nonzero delay so the clamp is not passing by making everything slow.
killedBy: difficulty moves the whole hazard picture, monotonically never lets HARD reach a current picture, however extreme the profile
